description: Severity distribution for breathing hazards — oxygen deprivation, toxic atmosphere, drowning/submersion, and asphyxiation. Distinct from chemical (skin/ingestion exposure) and structural_collapse (burial). The common thread is interruption of breathing — whether by absence of oxygen, presence of toxic gas, or submersion. P(death) scale from AIS mortality data.
magnitude_note: Breathing hazards are binary in a way other mechanisms are not — consciousness is lost within seconds to minutes of oxygen deprivation, and death follows within minutes if not rescued. The dose-response is less about magnitude and more about exposure duration and rescue speed. Bands are by hazard type because the onset speed and rescue window differ.

magnitude_bands.description: Nuisance dust, welding fume, mild irritant gas below acute threshold. Causes coughing, eye/throat irritation but no acute life threat. Chronic exposure causes occupational disease but that's not an acute SIF event.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: Occupational hygiene literature: nuisance exposure below OEL/WEL causes irritation, not acute injury. Chronic disease (silicosis, COPD) is a different risk framework.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Below acute thresholds, breathing hazards cause irritation only. P90=first_aid reflects eye washing, fresh air recovery. Not an acute SIF event. Chronic disease risk is real but outside the SIF framework (it's an occupational health issue, not a safety event).

magnitude_bands.description: Acute toxic gas or vapour exposure above IDLH. H2S, CO, chlorine, ammonia, HCN, phosgene. Rapid onset of symptoms, can cause collapse within breaths at high concentrations.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: NIOSH IDLH documentation; CSB toxic release investigations; H2S fatality data (OSHA: H2S is the leading cause of acute inhalation death in the workplace). CO poisoning mortality ~1-3% for those reaching hospital, much higher for unrescued.
magnitude_bands.rationale: H2S at >100ppm causes olfactory fatigue (can't smell it), at >500ppm causes immediate collapse. CO is insidious — no warning, progressive incapacitation. Chlorine/ammonia cause pulmonary oedema. P50=serious_injury reflects hospitalisation for inhalation injury. P90=fatality from sustained exposure without rescue. IDLH means 'immediately dangerous to life' — the name says it.

magnitude_bands.description: Oxygen-deficient atmosphere (<19.5% O2). Confined space with inert gas displacement (N2, CO2, Ar), biological oxygen consumption (fermentation, decomposition), or simple displacement. The classic confined space killer.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: HSE confined space fatality data; OSHA permit-required confined space incidents. Oxygen-deficient atmospheres cause ~60% of confined space fatalities. At <16% O2 impaired judgement, <10% unconsciousness in seconds, <6% death within minutes.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Oxygen-deficient atmospheres are lethally deceptive — no smell, no warning. At <10% O2, unconsciousness occurs in 1-2 breaths. The victim collapses, rescuers enter without SCBA and collapse too (multiple-fatality cascade is the signature pattern). P10=medical_treatment reflects momentary exposure with rapid self-rescue. P50 reflects the high fatality rate once incapacitation occurs — rescue requires SCBA-equipped team.

magnitude_bands.description: Drowning or submersion. Fall into water, flooding, working over/near water without PFD. Also includes engulfment in grain, sand, or other flowable material (similar mechanism — material fills airway).
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: WHO drowning data; OSHA maritime/construction fatality data; grain engulfment studies (Purdue University: ~50% fatality rate for grain engulfment). Drowning is the 3rd leading cause of unintentional death globally.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Submersion produces unconsciousness in 1-3 minutes, brain death in 4-6 minutes. Survival depends entirely on rescue speed and water temperature (cold water extends the window slightly). Grain engulfment is worse — no buoyancy, victim sinks. P10 reflects near-drowning with rapid rescue. P50 reflects the narrow rescue window.

magnitude_bands.description: Confined space with combined hazards — oxygen deficiency + toxic gas + limited escape. Tanks, vessels, sewers, manholes, silos, ship holds. The worst-case breathing scenario: multiple hazards, limited access, cascading rescuer casualties.
magnitude_bands.mortality_source: HSE confined space fatality data: 15-20 confined space deaths/year in UK. OSHA: confined space entry is the #1 cause of multiple-fatality events in general industry. 60% of confined space deaths are would-be rescuers.
magnitude_bands.rationale: Confined spaces combine every breathing hazard with limited escape and delayed rescue. The cascade pattern (worker enters → collapses → colleague enters to rescue → also collapses) makes these disproportionately multi-fatality events. P10=serious_injury reflects the rare case where atmospheric monitoring triggers alarm before full exposure. Without monitoring, entry into a toxic/oxygen-deficient confined space is near-uniformly fatal.

warning_properties.description: Multiplier on P(death). Gases with strong warning properties (ammonia, chlorine) prompt self-rescue. Odourless gases (CO, N2, CO2, inert gases) give no warning — olfactory fatigue with H2S makes it odourless at high concentrations despite strong smell at low concentrations.

rescue_capability.description: Multiplier on P(death). Breathing hazards are uniquely time-critical — brain damage begins at 4 minutes without oxygen. SCBA-equipped rescue team on standby transforms the survival probability. Untrained bystander rescue attempts frequently produce additional casualties.

concentration_duration.description: Multiplier on P(death). For toxic gases, dose = concentration × time. Brief exposure may cause symptoms without incapacitation. Sustained exposure at IDLH+ is almost always fatal without respiratory protection.

sources.author: HSE
sources.relevance: Confined Spaces Regulations 1997 guidance. 15-20 UK confined space deaths/year. 60% of deaths are would-be rescuers.

sources.author: OSHA
sources.relevance: Permit-Required Confined Spaces standard (29 CFR 1910.146). Confined space is #1 cause of multiple-fatality events in general industry.

sources.author: NIOSH
sources.relevance: IDLH documentation for toxic gases. Worker Deaths in Confined Spaces report. Criteria for immediately dangerous concentrations.

sources.author: Purdue University
sources.relevance: Grain engulfment data — ~50% fatality rate. Entrapment in flowing grain behaves like quicksand.

sources.author: WHO
sources.relevance: Global drowning data — 3rd leading cause of unintentional death. Submersion survival times by water temperature.

sources.author: Baker et al.

validation_notes: STKY check: confined space entry without monitoring should give P(SIF) near 1.0 — confined_space_combined P(SIF)=0.90 ✓
STKY check: H2S exposure above IDLH should give P(SIF) > 0.50 — toxic_gas_acute P(SIF)=0.50 ✓
STKY check: fall into water without PFD should give P(SIF) > 0.50 — drowning_submersion P(SIF)=0.72 ✓
Cross-check: welding fume exposure is NON_SIF — nuisance_dust_fume P(SIF)=0.000 ✓

Key insight: 60% of confined space deaths are rescuers, not the original entrant. The cascade rescue pattern is THE signature of confined space fatalities. This is why permit-to-work and standby rescue exist.

Overlap note: trench collapse burial → use structural_collapse (mechanism is burial/crush). Confined space with toxic atmosphere → use this (mechanism is breathing). Some real events involve both — the model picks the dominant mechanism from the narrative.
Overlap note: cryogenic oxygen displacement (LN2, CO2) → could be classified as thermal (cryogenic) or breathing (O2 deficiency). The lethal mechanism is usually the O2 displacement, not the cold.
